review_candidates.title: Program Manager
review_candidates.description: About Darkroom Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact. At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow, a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey. Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio. What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom's role as a defining player in the future of media innovation. About The Role This is a dedicated role on a single account, helping a key client bring a brand new product to market, with Darkroom owning all media channels. You are the operational owner of that engagement: the person accountable for the program running on time, in scope, and against every commitment, with no slips in timeline. That makes this different from a typical agency PM job. You are not coordinating a portfolio. You are going deep on one enterprise client, holding the operating rhythm, and creating accountability within the layers of Darkroom. You will report to the Director of Growth Strategy on the Hark engagement, with a dotted line to the Managing Director, Paid Media. You will work daily with Paid Social and Paid Search Specialists, Analytics, Creative, and the client's own program leads. This is a fully remote role supporting a team in the EST time zone (9 AM–5 PM EST). What You'll Do Service level accountability. You track our contracted SLAs, produce the reporting that evidences adherence, and escalate early when something is trending toward a miss. When the client asks whether we hit our commitments, the answer comes from you and it is already documented. The Shared Model. You maintain Darkroom's side of the jointly held media plan, forecast, and ramp model, keep it reconciled against actuals, and manage the cadence with the client's team so both sides are always working off the same numbers. Scope and budget control. You own hours tracking, scope-versus-delivered reconciliation, and ensuring we stay within scope. The operating rhythm. Standups, client status calls, internal syncs, QBR prep. Decisions, action items, and blockers documented and visible to both sides. Cross-functional handoffs. Briefs, assets, performance reporting, and campaign builds moving between Media, Creative, and Analytics on schedule, with dependencies mapped. Resourcing and capacity. Working with the Director of Growth Strategy and team leads to keep staffing matched to the work, and surfacing capacity risk before it shows up as a slipped deadline. Risk escalation. You are the point of escalation for cross-team dependencies and you keep stakeholders aligned without routing every conversation through leadership. You Should Apply If This Sounds Like You You have 3-5+ years of project or program management experience, ideally at a media, marketing, creative, or digital agency You're conversant in paid media workflows and terminology: campaign builds, flight dates, creative rotations, reporting cadences, even if you've never bought media yourself You build the tracker before someone asks for it, and you notice when a timeline is about to slip before anyone else does You're a clear, proactive communicator, comfortable managing up, across, and with clients when needed You are a Notion guru. Notion is Darkroom’s spine, and one needs to be fluent in Notion. This means designing and maintaining relational databases, building filtered views, and maintaining SOPs. You're comfortable working across Slack, Toggl, and Google Sheets-based trackers as your daily toolkit You can juggle multiple accounts and shifting priorities without dropping details You hold a high bar for your own output and expect the same from the people you coordinate with What It's Like To Work At Darkroom Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable. We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics. Unlimited PTO + Local holidays (Relevant to your hub): Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp. Remote-First Culture: Many roles are fully remote. Employees based in or near our New York or Lisbon HQs are expected to work hybrid with weekly in-office time. Hub locations include the Brazil and Spain. Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition. Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry. Equal Opportunity Statement Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

review_candidates.title: Global Roster of Early Childhood Development Specialists (Various Areas of Expertise), ECD Team, Global Programme Division, Remote, Req # 595680
review_candidates.description: Apply now Job no: 595680 Contract type: Consultant Duty Station: Nairobi Level: Consultancy Location: Kenya Categories: Early Childhood Development Consultancy: ROSTER: Early Childhood Development Specialists (Various Areas of Expertise) Section/Division/Duty Station: Early Childhood Development Team, GPD, Remote based Duration: 2026-2029 About UNICEF If you are a committed, creative professional and are passionate about making a lasting difference for children, the world's leading children's rights organization would like to hear from you. For 70 years, UNICEF has been working on the ground in 190 countries and territories to promote children's survival, protection and development. The world's largest provider of vaccines for developing countries, UNICEF supports child health and nutrition, good water and sanitation, quality basic education for all boys and girls, and the protection of children from violence, exploitation, and AIDS. UNICEF is funded entirely by the voluntary contributions of individuals, businesses, foundations and governments. UNICEF has over 12,000 staff in more than 145 countries. BACKGROUND Purpose Of Activity/ Assignment ECD is a fundamental right for every child. The Convention on the Rights of the Child recognizes the importance of supporting children’s survival, growth, development, protection, and participation from the earliest years of life. Under the Strategic Plan (2026-2029), UNICEF positions ECD as a strategic priority. ECD is now explicitly featured under Impact Result 1 of UNICEF’s Strategic Plan and has a designated sublevel target, as outlined below: Impact Result 1: 10 million child lives saved and at least 500 million children healthy, well-nourished, and developmentally on track Sub-level Result: 400 million children under 5 years of age benefitting from early stimulation, nurturing care, childcare services, and parenting support, including children with disabilities, by 2029. To achieve this ambition, UNICEF will apply a dual-path approach that combines dedicated ECD programme strengthening with mainstreaming early stimulation across sectors. Together, these pathways build a coherent and resilient ECD ecosystem so that early stimulation is both widely delivered and systemically embedded. Purpose Of The Roster To help achieve the results set out in UNICEF’s Strategic Plan and respond to growing demand from country offices and government partners for technical support on ECD, UNICEF is establishing a Global Roster of ECD Expert Consultants. The roster will play a central role in supporting UNICEF’s Centers of Excellence work on ECD by providing Country Offices with timely access to specialized expertise. The roster will function as a stand-by mechanism, enabling UNICEF to rapidly mobilize pre-qualified experts to provide timely and quality support on ECD. The Roster Will Encompass Three Complementary Areas Of Expertise, Aligned With The Three Areas Of UNICEF’s Vision For Early Childhood Development 2030 Area 1: Policies and legislation that enable opportunities for ECD Area 2: Programmes and services that protect, promote, and support ECD Area 3: Support to parents and caregivers in caring for their young children and themselves All outputs under this roster will align with the UNICEF Strategic Plan (2026–2029), reinforcing the CoE’s leadership in advancing ECD for children worldwide. Depending on the needs of the consultancy, expertise may be required in one or more of the areas listed above. Note Please note that inclusion in the roster does not imply automatic employment, compensation, deployment or guarantee any type of formal engagement with UNICEF. Most assignments will be home-based with possible travel depending on country requirements. Scope Of Work Under the Global Roster of ECD Experts, UNICEF seeks qualified consultants to provide technical expertise in at least one of the following areas. Applicants may apply to one or more areas of expertise: Areas of Expertise and Responsibilities Area 1: Policies and legislation that enable opportunities for ECD Key responsibilities: Technical expertise is needed in: Supporting the development and strengthening of multisectoral ECD policies/frameworks and costed action plans Advising on strengthened ECD governance and coordination mechanisms Advising on ECD financing mechanisms including public finance for ECD as well as innovative/hybrid modalities Developing ECD monitoring and evaluation frameworks, including advising on ECD M&E tools and indicators Advising on public-private partnerships for ECD/childcare Area 2: Programmes and services that protect, promote, and support ECD Key responsibilities: Technical expertise is needed in programme design, planning, implementation, M&E and scale-up of ECD programmes, with a focus on the following areas: Integration of early stimulation, responsive caregiving, and play into sectoral platforms (e.g., health, nutrition, protection, education) ECD interventions in emergencies Disability inclusion/ Early Childhood Intervention Childcare services Digital tools and innovations for ECD Area 3: Support to parents and caregivers in caring for their young children and themselves Key responsibilities: Technical expertise needed in policies and programme planning, design, implementation, M&E, and scale-up support with a focus on: Parenting support programmes for ECD including digital/hybrid modalities of support Caregiver mental health programmes with a focus on ECD Adolescent parents Evaluation of Applicants Only applicants who submit a complete application and meet the minimum eligibility requirements will be considered for further evaluation. Reference checks and academic credential verification will be conducted for shortlisted candidates as part of the selection process. Applicants accepted onto the roster will be eligible for direct recruitment by UNICEF offices for short-term consultancy assignments over a period of three years. When a need arises , UNICEF offices will contact suitable roster consultants with specific Terms of Reference outlining the scope and duration of the assignment and will confirm interest, availability, and the applicable fee. Qualifications Terms of Reference / Key Deliverables: Education Advanced university degree (Masters' degree) in Early Childhood Development, International Development, Developmental Psychology, Education, Global Health or related fields Knowledge/Expertise/Skills Required General Requirements (All Areas of Expertise) Minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible professional experience in international development. Minimum of 8 years of specialized experience in Early Childhood Development at the global level. Strong technical writing/communication skills and research skills, including demonstrated experience producing reports, case studies/documentation, and academic articles. Strong capacity to ensure quality, internal coherence, and timely revision of deliverables in response to internal and donor feedback. Willingness to participate in technical consultations, validation processes, and virtual or in-person missions, as required. Demonstrated commitment to knowledge sharing, documentation of lessons learned, and capacity strengthening related to ECD. Experience working collaboratively with multi-disciplinary teams, including UN staff, government counterparts, and development partners highly desirable. Experience in supporting resource mobilization efforts highly desirable Specific Requirements (Per Area of Expertise) Area 1: Policies and legislation that enable opportunities for ECD Candidates must meet at least 3 out of the 5 requirements below to be considered for this Area. Demonstrated experience advising/supporting development of ECD policies, frameworks, costed action plans, and/or M&E frameworks Demonstrated experience conducting ECD scoping/landscape analyses or ECD investment cases Demonstrated experience working on projects/initiatives focused on ECD financing mechanisms Demonstrated experience working on public-private partnerships for ECD Demonstrated experience producing global or regional reports on ECD trends and data Area 2: Programmes and services that protect, promote, and support ECD Candidates must meet at least 3 out of the 5 requirements below to be considered for this Area. Demonstrated experience working with governments/national partners at country level to design and implement ECD programmes Demonstrated experience developing ECD training packages for front-line workers Demonstrated experience conducting trainings (e.g., TOT, front-line worker trainings) on ECD packages and tools Demonstrated experience working on at least one of the four areas listed below: ECD interventions in emergencies Disability inclusion/ Early Childhood Intervention Childcare services Digital tools and innovations for ECD Demonstrated experience conducting research and/or writing technical reports/documentation on ECD programmes Area 3: Support to parents and caregivers in caring for their young children and themselves Candidates must meet at least 3 out of the 5 requirements below to be considered for this Area. Demonstrated experience developing and/or implementing parenting for ECD programmes and tools Demonstrated experience developing parenting support for ECD training packages for front-line workers Demonstrated experience delivering trainings on parenting support for ECD packages (e.g. TOT, front-line worker trainings) Demonstrated experience adapting/contextualizing parenting programmes to local contexts Demonstrated experience conducting research and/or writing technical reports/documentation on parenting for ECD programmes Requirements Completed profile in UNICEF's e-Recruitment system and A curriculum vitae (CV) A cover letter A document listing relevant areas of expertise (from the sub-areas listed above), level of expertise, supporting evidence, and the proposed daily rate (applications without a daily rate will not be considered). Please indicate clearly which Area(s) of Expertise you are applying to. The names and contact details of three professional references (applications submitted without references will not be considered) Upload copy of academic credentials Financial proposal Any emergent / unforeseen duty travel and related expenses will be covered by UNICEF. At the time the contract is awarded, the selected candidate must have in place current health insurance coverage. Payment of professional fees will be based on submission of agreed satisfactory deliverables. UNICEF reserves the right to withhold payment in case the deliverables submitted are not up to the required standard or in case of delays in submitting the deliverables on the part of the consultant. U.S. Visa Information With the exception of the US Citizens, G4 Visa and Green Card holders, should the selected candidate and his/her household members reside in the United States under a different visa, the consultant and his/her household members are required to change their visa status to G4, and the consultant’s household members (spouse) will require an Employment Authorization Card (EAD) to be able to work, even if he/she was authorized to work under the visa held prior to switching to G4. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process For every Child, you demonstrate… UNICEF’s core values of Commitment, Diversity and Integrity and core competencies in Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results. View our competency framework at: Here UNICEF offers reasonable accommodation for consultants/individual contractors with disabilities. This may include, for example, accessible software, travel assistance for missions or personal attendants. We encourage you to disclose your disability during your application in case you need reasonable accommodation during the selection process and afterwards in your assignment. UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination. UNICEF also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. All selected candidates will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles and will therefore undergo rigorous reference and background checks. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check. Remarks Individuals engaged under a consultancy will not be considered “staff members” under the Staff Regulations and Rules of the United Nations and UNICEF’s policies and procedures and will not be entitled to benefits provided therein (such as leave entitlements and medical insurance coverage). Their conditions of service will be governed by their contract and the General Conditions of Contracts for the Services of Consultants. Consultants are responsible for determining their tax liabilities and for the payment of any taxes and/or duties, in accordance with local or other applicable laws. The selected candidate is solely responsible to ensure that the visa (applicable) and health insurance required to perform the duties of the contract are valid for the entire period of the contract. Selected candidates are subject to confirmation of fully-vaccinated status against SARS-CoV-2 (Covid-19) with a World Health Organization (WHO)-endorsed vaccine, which must be met prior to taking up the assignment. It does not apply to consultants who will work remotely and are not expected to work on or visit UNICEF premises, programme delivery locations or directly interact with communities UNICEF works with, nor to travel to perform functions for UNICEF for the duration of their consultancy contracts.
